target_customer: K-12 teachers and school administrators; schools pay $5 per user per month on the school plan
problem: Teachers duplicated curriculum work and lacked shared, standards-aligned materials.
business_model: Nonprofit; free plans, paid school plan $5 per user per month, network plans (company site)
product_category: K-12 curriculum planning library and tool

technical_complexity.rationale: Content library and planning software; standard web engineering.

defensibility.rationale: Open, community curated content with no stated moat.

market_need_then: No dated evidence read; the company positions itself around free community resources for K-12 education.

branding.name_origin: Open plus curriculum, descriptive of the open library (inference from the nonprofit's mission, not a founder statement)

brand_strength.rationale: Descriptive name; no brand evidence read.

pivots.from: Open library of community curated teaching materials
pivots.to: Lesson, unit and course planning tool with standards alignment (current site)

outcome_analysis: OpenCurriculum is an active 501(c)3 nonprofit from Winter 2014 that has moved from a community library toward a planning tool with a paid school tier. No funding, traction or exit data was found, so the outcome is unclear: it has survived at least twelve years but with no evidence of scale.
